prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map shows a plastered wall directly in front of the camera wearer (~0.3 to 1.0 m away) in frames 1, 2, and 5, while in frames 3 and 4 the camera tilts downward to show rough rubble ground (~1.0 to 1.5 m below) with two adjacent round mortar pans (~0.6 to 1.0 m away, ~0.1 m apart) and a white PVC pipe descending from the upper right (~0.3 to 0.8 m away). In frame 3, the camera wearer's right hand enters at the bottom edge (~0.4 m away) within arm's reach to grasp the rim of the central mortar pan, and in frame 4 lifts the pan closer (~0.4 to 0.6 m away) so it partially occludes the ground and the second pan at the bottom left. In frame 5, the camera turns upward and right toward the wall corner (~0.4 m away on the left with twin vertical pipes), revealing a man standing on the right (~1.2 to 1.5 m from the camera wearer and ~0.5 m to the right of the wall corner) facing sideways to the left with his head angled slightly downward rather than looking directly at the camera wearer, with his lower legs cropped out of view and his right hand within arm's reach of the wall corner. The depth gradient clearly separates the elevated foreground mortar pan and protruding PVC pipe from the recessed rubble ground and wall corner in a way that is flatter in the RGB image alone. However, the map is per-frame scale-normalized and unreliable in frame 1 and 2 where the flat wall's upper right is rendered bright white as if nearer than the base, and in frame 5 where the background street and trees behind the man drop abruptly to pure black.
descriptions.segmentation: The instance segmentation map is completely blank in frames 1 and 2, detects only the protruding end of the white PVC pipe in the upper right of frames 3 and 4 (~0.3 to 0.8 m away, above and to the right of the mortar pans on the ground), and in frame 5 detects the man standing on the right (~1.2 to 1.5 m away, to the right of the wall corner). In frame 5, the pink person mask outlines the man from head to upper thighs—capturing his left-facing profile, forward-extended right hand near the wall corner, and torso—while his lower legs are truncated by the bottom frame edge. Across the 5 frames, the segmented regions track the camera wearer tilting down toward the pipe and ground in frames 3–4 (where the pipe appears larger and closer in frame 4 as the camera moves) and then turning up and right to face the man at the wall corner in frame 5. The crisp pink mask in frame 5 isolates the man's silhouette and extended right hand cleanly from the cluttered background trees, sunlit street, and motorcycle that blend together in the RGB image. However, the map is highly unreliable across the sequence because it misclassifies the white PVC pipe as a 'knife' in frames 3 and 4, completely misses the camera wearer's hand in frame 3, and fails to segment any of the mortar pans, walls, or pipes in frames 1–5.
descriptions.pose: The pose map contains no detections in frames 1 through 4 and renders a single yellow body skeleton in frame 5 for the man standing on the right (~1.2 to 1.5 m from the camera wearer and ~0.5 m to the right of the plastered wall). A cluster of five facial keypoints at the top right indicates his head is angled toward the left and slightly downward toward the ground/wall base rather than looking directly at the camera wearer, while the torso rectangle and left arm segments show his upper body turned in left profile with his left arm hanging down to a cluster of yellow wrist/finger keypoints near the bottom right edge (within arm's reach of his hip and a wooden pole behind him). Across the 5 frames, the absence of skeletons in frames 1–4 and the appearance of the man on the right in frame 5 reflect the camera wearer looking at the wall, tilting down to pick up the mortar pan, and turning right toward the wall corner where the man stands partially cut off below the hips. The skeleton in frame 5 makes the man's shoulder alignment, torso tilt, and left elbow-to-wrist geometry explicit despite his loose pink shirt and dark trousers in the RGB frame. However, the pose map is unreliable where it completely misses the camera wearer's visible right hand reaching for the pan in frame 3, omits the man's extended right arm and legs in frame 5, and provides no magenta hand skeletons in any frame.
